question: Which Xbox-native unit-definition field owns normal production base cost, how is its effective value composed, and which bounded completion, display, and AI paths consume it?

scope.boundary: This topic closes the normal unit production factor, the separate ID-100-through-199 and ID-200-through-299 base-cost fields, the unit scalar, two cost wrappers, one completion threshold, the accepted rush-area display consumer, and two accepted AI input consumers. It does not assign complete record layouts or identities to the two non-unit tables, establish their complete modifier composition, prove general UI or AI parity, map downstream completion effects, claim runtime execution, or define an implementation contract.

dependencies.use: Accepted unit-definition table, stride, record identities, and AI function identities
Accepted unit rush producer, display owner, command path, and apply boundary
Accepted active Unique Era Ability lookup and bonus ID meanings where available

baseCostField.qualification: The byte is a factor, not the final production cost. Adjacent bytes at +0x45 through +0x47 remain unnamed, and this packet does not catalogue the other 21 factor values.

nonUnitBaseCostFields.commonPath: Both range-specific signed fields multiply the helper's current scalar and join at 0x82CF1330 before later modifiers.
nonUnitBaseCostFields.qualification: Existing wrapper terminology identifies the two ranges as building and wonder production items. This bounded storage packet does not recover record names, counts, complete layouts, every field value, complete modifier ownership, or runtime execution.

inputs.playerIndexedValue: signed halfword at 0x830E9050 + player*2; semantic owner unresolved
inputs.item: signed city halfword +0x38 unless argument two supplies an override

composition: Start at ten; if the player-indexed value is positive, subtract it from ten.
If neutral condition 0x82CEF4E8(14) is nonzero, subtract one quarter of the current scalar with signed round-toward-zero arithmetic.
If unit-definition +0x50 bit zero is set and bonus 5 is active, subtract one half of the current scalar.
For unit types 10, 6, and 28, active bonus IDs 17, 33, and 34 respectively subtract one half of the current scalar. Bonus 33 remains semantically unresolved.
effectiveScalar.normalUnitCost: signed definition factor at +0x44 multiplied by the returned scalar, then divided by two with signed round-toward-zero arithmetic
effectiveScalar.qualification: Condition 14, the player-indexed halfword owner, and bonus 33 remain neutral. The helper handles only item IDs 0 through 99; this is static composition, not runtime proof.

costWrappers.result: Returns -1 for item -1, uses the unit factor and scalar for IDs 0 through 99, and routes IDs 100 through 299 through BuildingWonderProductionCostLookup at 0x82CF1278.
Reads current city item +0x38, returns zero outside IDs 0 through 299, and otherwise uses the unit formula or BuildingWonderProductionCostLookup at 0x82CF1278.

rushProducer.result: The unit branch composes full normal unit cost, subtracts signed invested production at city +0x36, and then applies the separately accepted rush-gold arithmetic.
rushProducer.qualification: This establishes the normal-cost input to rush calculation, not complete rush-modifier composition or RushApply parity.

display.result: The accepted rush-area display owner calls CurrentProductionItemCostLookup, then uses signed city fields +0x36 and +0x42 with the positive returned cost in separate percentage calculations.
display.qualification: This is one exact rush-area display consumer, not general normal production UI parity.

completion.result: The unit branch compares signed invested production at city +0x36 with the composed full unit cost and branches away while invested production is less.
completion.qualification: The fallthrough enters a larger item-processing body. Unit creation, overflow, queue changes, and other completion paths remain unresolved.

ai.result: Directly consumes helper 0x82CF1148 and signed definition +0x44, then combines those inputs with invested production and the local bonus-25 and bonus-35 rush arithmetic.
ai.qualification: The local ordering differs from the standalone normal-cost wrappers; no AI decision parity or corrected rush parity is claimed.

ai.result: Directly consumes helper 0x82CF1148 and signed definition +0x44 and applies signed half scaling.
ai.qualification: The enclosing score and decision effect remain unresolved.

guards: Treat +0x44 as a signed normal unit production factor, not a direct final-cost byte.
Keep unit, ID-100-through-199, and ID-200-through-299 production fields separate; the three ranges use distinct tables, strides, widths, and offsets.
Do not infer complete building or wonder record layouts, names, counts, modifier ownership, or field values from the two base-cost accesses.
Do not name adjacent definition bytes +0x45 through +0x47 or the player-indexed scalar owner from proximity.
Do not infer general AI parity from two direct input consumers; strategy, scoring, choice, corrected rush behavior, and every other AI path remain unresolved.
Do not infer general UI parity from the accepted rush-area display consumer.
Do not infer complete production completion behavior from the one invested-versus-cost threshold.
Do not infer runtime execution, production behavior, API suitability, or implementation safety from static evidence.
conclusion: Version 1.3 stores a signed normal unit production base-cost factor at unit-definition offset +0x44. Exact helper 0x82CF1148 composes a player- and unit-sensitive scalar, and the normal unit cost is factor times scalar divided by two. Separate helper 0x82CF1278 reads IDs 100 through 199 from signed byte +0x41 of 0xCC-byte records at 0x82F71FD8 and IDs 200 through 299 from signed halfword +0x40 of 0x14C-byte records at 0x82F73238. Two wrappers expose the applicable value, while the bounded rush producer, rush-area display owner, one unit completion threshold, AIUnitChoiceEvaluate, and AITurnUnitEvaluation consume the unit field or composed value. Complete non-unit record layouts and modifiers, runtime behavior, full UI, complete completion, rush-apply, and general AI parity remain unresolved.
